title: Solution score from step scores
goal:
A PRM gives each step three label probabilities. The paper turns them into one score per solution so that it can rank solutions (Section 2.6 and Appendix F.2). Write two functions:

- `step_scores(p_pos, p_neu, neutral="positive")` takes the per-step probabilities of the positive and neutral labels (two sequences of the same length) and returns a float array with one score per step. With `neutral="positive"` the score is `p_pos + p_neu`. With `neutral="negative"` it is `p_pos`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- `solution_score(p_pos, p_neu, neutral="positive", reduction="product")` returns a Python float. With `reduction="product"` it is the product of the step scores, the paper's choice. With `reduction="min"` it is the smallest step score. Any other `reduction`, or a solution with no steps, raises `ValueError`.
hints: Convert the inputs with `np.asarray(..., dtype=float)` first, so lists and arrays both work.
The probability that every step is correct is the product of the step probabilities. A solution with 10 steps at 0.98 scores $0.98^{10} \approx 0.817$ under the product and $0.98$ under the minimum.
`np.prod` and `np.min` fail on or misbehave with empty input, so check `scores.size` before you reduce and raise `ValueError`.
Wrap the result in `float(...)` so that the caller gets a Python float and not a NumPy scalar.
